fact: The document is Cameroon's National Strategy for the Development of Statistics (SNDS30) 2021-2030, Volume 1 strategy paper, issued by the National Statistics Council and the INS, with a priority action plan 2021-2025; it gives no adoption date, so the published date (2021, year only) is used.

Cameroon Tribune reports the HISWACA project steering committee met to support implementation of the Statistics Development Strategy 2020-2030, which is thus in force; the article gives no adoption date, so the article date is used.
PARIS21's January 2026 NSDS status table lists the strategy as implementing (adopted): SNDS 2021-2030.

The INS says the third-generation SNDS was adopted in 2021, with a five-year action plan costed at about FCFA 63 billion for 2021-2025, presented to technical and financial partners at a workshop on 6 April 2022.
The INS said in June 2023 that the SNDS was evaluated in 2022; the evaluation's month is not given.

EcoMatin reported on 26 June 2024 that the SNDS30 financing plan sets a budget of FCFA 166.5 billion for 2024-2028, with FCFA 68.9 billion from the state, 63.3 billion from the World Bank and a 34.1 billion gap.
